settings.core.reference_check.descriptio: Checks file references in cores that are missing or can no longer be found.
settings.help.tutorial.description: Open the three-step tutorial again. It does not create test files or change your current layout.

settings.advanced.data_folder.descriptio: The program data folder contains state, backups, and logs. Do not delete files you do not recognize.
settings.advanced.report.description: Problem reports contain only redacted runtime logs and window state. Nothing is uploaded.

dialog.restore_relations.title: Restore previous workspace relationships
dialog.restore_relations.message:
A previous Gravity Desktop workspace was found.

You can restore {coreCount} Cores and {fileCount} file references. Restoring only recreates visual relationships; it never moves, copies, or deletes real files.
dialog.restore_relations.footer: Keeping the current Desktop is the default. No choice changes real files.
dialog.restore_relations.failed: Restore failed. The current Desktop was not changed.
dialog.restore_relations.partial_failed: Partial restore failed. The current Desktop was not changed.
dialog.store.title: Store in Core
dialog.store.message: Store "{file}" in "{core}"? It will be moved from the Desktop and can be restored at any time.
dialog.store.public_message: Store "{file}" in "{core}"? It will be moved from the Public Desktop, so other Windows users will no longer see this shortcut. It can be restored at any time.
dialog.store.footer: After confirmation, further files can be stored without asking again for 10 minutes.
dialog.store.public_footer: Public Desktop items always require confirmation.
dialog.store_batch.title: Store existing Desktop references
dialog.store_batch.message: Store these {count} existing Desktop references in "{core}"? After success, they will be removed from the Windows Desktop and kept in the Gravity Desktop library.
dialog.store_batch.public_suffix: {count} item(s) are on the Public Desktop, so other Windows users will no longer see them.
dialog.store_batch.footer: The files are committed as one batch. If any item fails, the entire batch rolls back to its pre-operation state.
dialog.dissolve.title: Dissolve Core and restore files to Desktop
dialog.dissolve.message:
Dissolve Core "{core}"?

{managedCount} managed file(s) will be restored to the Windows Desktop; other files only lose their right-side reference.
Real files will not be deleted.
dialog.dissolve.unclassified_message:
Clear {referenceCount} references from Uncategorized?

{managedCount} managed file(s) will be restored to the Windows Desktop; other references only lose their right-side node. Real files will not be deleted.
dialog.delete_core.title: Remove Core and all references
dialog.delete_core.message:
Remove Core "{core}" and its {count} file reference(s) from Gravity Desktop?

Real files will not be affected.
dialog.managed_protection.title: Managed file protection
dialog.managed_protection.message:
This Core contains stored real files.

To ensure every file keeps a normal Desktop entry, these references cannot be discarded directly.
Choosing Confirm dissolves the Core and restores all managed files to the Windows Desktop; Cancel keeps the current Core.
recovery.manifest_error:
The recovery manifest could not be read. No files were moved.

Make sure the Gravity Desktop library is still intact.
recovery.no_files: No managed files need to be restored.
recovery.desktop_error: The current Windows Desktop location could not be read.
recovery.already_restored: All managed files have already been restored to the Windows Desktop.
recovery.prompt:
Found {count} file(s) managed by Gravity Desktop.

Restore them to the Windows Desktop?
Core relationship records will be kept and can be imported again later.
recovery.journal_error: The recovery transaction log could not be written. No files were moved.
recovery.main_running:
Gravity Desktop is still running. Exit it safely before emergency recovery.
No files were moved.

tutorial.step.collection: Step 2: Build a stable file collection
tutorial.body.create:
Click an empty area on the right or the + button to create a project Core.

Gravity Desktop creates file references only. It does not move, delete, or rename real files.
tutorial.body.collection: Drag files from the Windows Desktop or File Explorer into a Core. The real files stay in their original locations.
tutorial.body.open: Click a Core to see its files. Double-click a file to open it from its original path.
tutorial.skipped: Tutorial skipped. You can open it again from the system tray.
tutorial.completed: Tutorial complete. Start organizing your workspace.
empty_workspace.title: Create your first Core
empty_workspace.body: Drag frequently used files from the left into this area to build a stable work collection.
